questions.answer: Gravitational potential energy is energy stored by a mass because of its position or height in a gravitational field. Moving the zero-height level adds the same offset to both endpoint values, so their difference is unchanged.
accepted_alternatives: energy a mass has due to its position in a gravitational field, with the explanation that only the height difference between the two positions is used
questions.unit_policy: No unit required unless an energy value is introduced, in which case joule is required.
questions.tolerance: The controlled definition must retain energy, mass, position or height, and gravitational field.

marking_points.text: States gravitational potential energy as energy stored by a mass because of its position or height in a gravitational field
Explains that changing the zero-height level shifts both endpoint values equally so their energy difference is unchanged

questions.answer: At constant speed the lifting force balances weight, so F = mg = 7.50 × 9.81 = 73.6 N. W = Fs = 73.575 × 1.80 = 132.435 J, so the gravitational potential energy increase is 132 J to three significant figures. A unit check gives N m = J, or direct substitution into mgΔh gives the same value.
accepted_alternatives: Accept 132.4 J if an extra significant figure is retained consistently.
questions.unit_policy: Force final answer requires N and energy final answer requires J.
questions.tolerance: Accept 73.5 N to 73.6 N and 132 J to 132.5 J with correct working.

questions.answer: The derivation uses zero acceleration to set F = mg, then W = Fs = mgΔh, and identifies this work with ΔE_P. For the panel, ΔE_P = 25.0 × 9.81 × 4.20 = 1030.05 J = 1.03 × 10^3 J. The relevant displacement for gravitational energy is the vertical height change because gravity and weight act vertically; the longer rail changes the force-distance pairing but not the endpoint height difference.
accepted_alternatives: Accept 1.03 kJ for the numerical result.
questions.unit_policy: Energy final answer requires J or kJ with a correct conversion.
questions.tolerance: Accept 1.03 × 10^3 J or 1.030 kJ to consistent significant figures.

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: Constant speed means zero acceleration and zero resultant force, so the lifting force equals weight: F = mg. With vertical displacement s = Δh, W = Fs = mgΔh. This work becomes the gravitational potential energy increase, so ΔE_P = mgΔh.
parts.unit_policy: No numerical unit required; symbol meanings must be consistent.
parts.tolerance: The argument must explicitly connect work, weight, vertical height and energy change.

Identifies the work done against gravity as the increase in gravitational potential energy and concludes ΔE_P = mgΔh

parts.answer: Weight acts vertically, so the displacement component in its direction is the 4.20 m vertical height change. The smooth rail changes the force and distance along the route but the gravitational potential energy change depends only on the fixed initial and final heights.
parts.unit_policy: No unit required for this explanation.
parts.tolerance: Both the vertical direction and endpoint-height reasoning are required for full credit.
